newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Judge suspends new Argentine telephone rates.
newsitem.headline: Judge suspends new Argentine telephone rates.

text.p: An Argentine judge ordered Friday the suspension of the government's recent changes to the country's telephone rates, which boosted local charges but drastically cut long-distance rates.
Judge Maria Jose Sarmiento ordered the suspension after Ombudsman Jorge Maiorano requested the rate changes be reversed, but said a final ruling was still to come.

"With this measure, the changes that came into effect Saturday will be suspended until the courts decide on the legality (of the legal challenge lodged by the Ombudsman)," a spokesman for the Ombudsman told Reuters.
Shares in telephone companies Telefnica de Argentina and Telecom de Argentina surged last week after last Friday's decree authorizing the rate changes.
ADRs in Telefnica fell 3/8 to 29-7/8 and Telecom slipped 3/4 to 47-1/4 on today's news.

The companies had waged a long and arduous campaign for the changes, arguing they would make charges fairer for business and help them become more competitive by the time the Argentine phone market is thrown open to all comers, probably in the year 2000.

Consumer groups and opposition parties fought hard against the changes, and argued in public hearings ending in December that private users' telephone bills would rise and the phone companies would pocket the difference.

The changes included the abolition of free local call time, boosted the prices of other local calls and increased monthly rental charges. At the same time, the cost of the longest distance domestic calls was cut by 56 percent and international call rates to major destinations were reduced by an average 42 percent.
